Bank 2 temperature comparison not possible
No noticeable change in driving
c: Lead of the rear bank 2 probe damaged

U0688.d: Throttle sensor G is the second track of a second throttle body. GM's 23OBDG07 and 24OBDG07 tables, for a program with one throttle per bank, use it for throttle position sensor 2 on bank 2.
s: Check engine light on the first trip
Reduced power, uneven running between banks
U0608 stored at the same time
c: SENT, supply or ground wire to the bank 2 throttle body faulty
Throttle body connector loose, wet or corroded
Sensor electronics in the throttle body failed (replaced as a unit)

U0689.d: Twin-charger engines may monitor a temperature at the second charger, for instance to protect the compressor or turbine of charger B from overheating; CARB's diesel data list includes compressor inlet as well as turbine inlet and outlet temperatures. U0689 means the reading of the temperature sensor for charger B arrives over a digital link and that link has failed.
s: Check engine light
Boost reduced as a precaution
Otherwise often unchanged driving
c: Wiring near charger B damaged by heat
Temperature sensor or its interface electronics failed

U068A.d: Barometric sensor C appears in two very different layouts. In GM's dual-throttle tables 23OBDG07/24OBDG07 it measures the air ahead of the bank 1 throttle; P227C and P227D judge its raw value (under 50 or over 115 kPa, 2 s), and U068A is set once the bank 1 SENT frames carry an incorrect length for 1.5 s, two trips to MIL.
s: Check engine light after two trips
Bank 1 fueling less precise
Accompanying pressure codes P227B to P227D possible
c: Signal, supply or ground wire to sensor C damaged
Connector at the intake pressure sensor loose or corroded

U068B.d: The inlet pressure sensor sits between air filter and compressor. Its reading shows filter restriction and, together with boost pressure, the pressure ratio the compressor works against.
s: Check engine light
Air filter restriction no longer monitored
Possibly somewhat reduced boost
c: SENT signal wire shorted to ground or voltage, or open
Connector on the intake duct loose, oily or corroded

U068C.d: A second inlet pressure sensor makes sense where each bank breathes through its own filter and charger, or where a two-stage system needs the pressure ahead of the second compressor. U068C means the digital frames from that sensor B no longer arrive in usable form.
s: Check engine light
Filter restriction on that side no longer detected
Slightly lower boost possible
c: Signal, supply or ground wire to inlet sensor B damaged
Connector loose or contaminated with oil

U068D.d: EGR temperature sensors show how hot the recirculated gas is, mostly behind the EGR cooler, so the controller can judge cooler efficiency and correct the gas density. U068D is the digital-link failure for sensor A.
s: Check engine light
EGR cooler monitoring not possible
c: Wiring to EGR temperature sensor A damaged near the cooler

U068E.d: GM documents this code in its 2025 diesel tables 25OBDG04A and 25OBDG04B, where sensor B is named EGR temperature sensor 1. Its circuit tests (P041C, P041D) are written for either a resistive probe or a digital thermocouple unit; the digital one counts as low below -72.8 °C.
s: Check engine light, on GM diesels in the first trip
Second code for the controller input stored alongside
EGR cooler efficiency not monitored
c: SENT signal, supply or ground wire to sensor B damaged
Internal fault in the sensor that shuts off its output
Connector corroded or contaminated by soot and oil
Fault at the controller input the sensor uses

U068F.d: Engines with both a high- and a low-pressure EGR loop need more temperature points, which is where slots C and D come in. U068F means the controller lost the digital messages of EGR temperature sensor C.
s: Check engine light
Low-pressure EGR reduced or disabled
c: Wiring to sensor C near the exhaust aftertreatment damaged

U0690.d: Sensor D is the last of the four EGR temperature slots, used only on systems with many measuring points, for example on both sides of a cooler in each of two EGR loops. U0690 says its digital messages have stopped reaching the controller.
s: Check engine light
EGR cooler check incomplete

U0691.d: On Ford's 6.7 L and 3.0 L diesels of 2023, exhaust pressure sensor A measures pressure ahead of the turbine and is a SENT device. Ford's diesel OBD summary sets U0691 when the low-level SENT driver sees a communication error or no data within the expected window, when the line is held at one voltage level, or when the sensor reports an internal fault; the check runs continuously and needs 5 s.
s: Check engine light
Reduced boost or power on some engines
EGR and turbo running on substitute values
c: SENT line shorted to ground or supply, or open, near the hot turbo
Sensor reports an internal error or stops sending
Sensor damaged by soot or condensate in the pressure line

U0692.d: Exhaust pressure sensor B is a second pressure point in the exhaust, whose location the maker defines, for instance on the other bank or behind the turbine. U0692 means its digital output, usually SENT, has stopped delivering valid frames.
s: Check engine light
Possibly reduced power
c: Wiring to pressure sensor B damaged by exhaust heat

U0693.d: Intake air humidity influences combustion temperature and NOx, so some engines measure it, usually with a capacitive element built into the air-mass meter; Bosch offers such meters with optional humidity sensing over SENT, FAS or LIN. GM's dual-throttle tables 23OBDG07/24OBDG07 use U0693 for a SENT humidity sensor on bank 1, stored when the sensor itself reports a maximum or minimum error for 1 s, MIL after two trips
s: Check engine light after two trips
Usually no noticeable drivability change
Accompanying humidity or air-mass codes possible
c: Humidity element in the air-mass meter contaminated or failed
Signal or supply wire to the sensor faulty
Moisture or corrosion in the connector

U0694.d: Liquid-cooled traction batteries rely on an electric pump to move coolant through the pack, and pumps like Bosch's PCE accept their speed command by PWM or LIN and report faults themselves. U0694 records that battery pump A no longer communicates.
s: Hybrid/EV system warning
Reduced drive power
Slower DC fast charging
c: Coolant entered the pump electronics housing
Bus, supply or ground wire to the pump damaged
Battery or hybrid controller software fault

U0695.d: Pump B is a second pump in the battery thermal circuit; what it serves, for instance a parallel branch or a heater or chiller loop, is up to the manufacturer. U0695 is set when that pump stops answering on its data link.
s: Battery temperature warning or power limit
Charging power reduced
Hybrid/EV system warning
c: Wiring or connector of pump B damaged or wet
Pump B electronics or motor failed

U0696.d: In GM's 2025 diesel tables 25OBDG04A and 25OBDG04B, sensor C is the downstream relative pressure sensor, which reads the gauge pressure behind the particulate filter and carries its own temperature element (lost communication there is U06B6). U0696 is set when the sensor reports message faults above a fixed count or when its newest message is too old, judged as 158 failures in 200 samples at 12.5 ms intervals.
s: Check engine light, on GM diesels in the first trip
Particulate filter regeneration based on estimates or delayed
c: Wiring to the downstream pressure sensor damaged by heat or chafing
Internal sensor fault that switches off the SENT output

U0697.d: Sensor D is the fourth filter pressure slot and appears only in Ford's 2024 gasoline OBD summary, which watches particulate filters on both banks (P226D and P226E for a missing substrate). There U0697 sits with P2CEA in the circuit and lost-communication check for SENT-type pressure sensors A to D: it runs all the time and needs 5 s to log a fault.
s: Check engine light
Particulate filter monitor for one bank incomplete
c: Wiring to filter pressure sensor D damaged

U0698.d: Coolant pump E continues the generic letter series of auxiliary electric pumps after A to D. Mercedes-Benz uses it for the second coolant pump in its low-temperature circuit: bulletin LI20.00-P-076708 lists U0698E4 and U0698E5 in the powertrain control unit N127 together with other LIN devices such as fan, charge-air cooler pump and high-temperature control valve.
s: Check engine light
Coolant warning message
Radiator fan running at full speed
c: Powertrain control unit software (Mercedes N127 version 22A)
LIN wiring or intermediate connector chafed or corroded

U0699.d: Pump F is the sixth auxiliary electric coolant pump in the generic lettering, and the code flags that this pump has stopped responding on its data line. No manufacturer documents U0699 publicly; even the Mercedes bulletin that uses the E code for a low-temperature pump lists no F.
s: Warning light depending on manufacturer
Loop served by pump F runs too warm
Radiator fan running more often or at full speed
c: Data, supply or ground wire to pump F damaged
Pump F electronics or motor failed

U069A.d: The third exhaust temperature sensor on bank 1 usually sits in the aftertreatment, ahead of the filter or SCR stage. GM covers U069A in both 2025 diesel tables, 25OBDG04A and 25OBDG04B: a SENT sensor whose output was switched off by an internal fault, or that sends faulty or outdated messages, fails the check once 19 readings out of 25, taken every 100 ms, are bad.
s: Check engine light, on GM diesels in the first trip
Particulate filter regeneration blocked or postponed
Further code for the controller input
c: Sensor harness along the aftertreatment burnt or chafed
Electronics module of the thermocouple sensor failed

U069B.d: Sensor 4 is the fourth temperature point along the bank 1 exhaust. Of GM's 2025 diesel tables only 25OBDG04A contains U069A's partner U069B; 25OBDG04B ends at sensor 3.
s: Check engine light
Regeneration interrupted or not started
c: Harness to sensor 4 damaged by heat during regeneration

U069C.d: U069C refers to the third temperature probe in the bank 2 exhaust path, so it can only occur where each cylinder bank feeds its own aftertreatment line, as on some V engines. Such a probe is a digital unit that reports its reading as SENT or CAN frames; the code is stored when those frames stop or keep failing their checks.
s: Check engine light
Filter regeneration on bank 2 postponed or blocked
Probe shows no value in live data
c: Sensor harness on the bank 2 exhaust side chafed or heat-damaged
Electronics box of the probe failed
Probe has lost its supply or ground

U069D.d: Sensor 4 is normally the final measuring position in the bank 2 exhaust, often placed further down the aftertreatment where the controller judges how hot the gas leaves the filter or catalyst stages. U069D reports that this digital probe has gone silent on its data link.
s: Check engine light
Regeneration delayed or cancelled
c: Probe lead melted or torn near the rear aftertreatment
Electronics unit of the probe dead
Supply fuse or feed wire of the probe faulty

U069E.d: Coolant heater A is an electric heater with its own control electronics that warms coolant for the cabin and, in some designs, for the traction battery – usually a high-voltage PTC unit in hybrids and EVs. The vehicle commands it over a data link, mostly LIN: DBK's 400 V heater is driven via LIN 2.0 plus a PWM input, and Webasto's 800 V range adds CAN on its larger models.
s: Little or no cabin heat in electric mode
Engine starts more often in cold weather to supply heat (hybrids)
Slow battery warm-up or reduced charging power in frost, where the heater serves the battery
c: LIN or CAN line to the heater broken, shorted or connector loose
12 V supply or ground of the heater electronics missing
Control electronics inside the heater failed
Heater or master module software fault

U069F.d: Exhaust pressure sensor C is a third pressure measuring point in the exhaust; where it sits is up to the manufacturer, for example behind the turbine or on a second exhaust branch. U069F: this digital sensor, typically a SENT device, no longer supplies usable frames.
s: Check engine light
Possibly less boost or power
Pressure value missing or frozen in live data
c: Signal, supply or ground wire of sensor C damaged by exhaust heat
Sensor C reports an internal fault or stops sending
Moisture or corrosion in the sensor connector
